sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Redmond, WA?
sections.html:
You can sell a Redmond house quickly by accepting a cash offer, listing it with an agent, or selling it yourself. The right route depends on how much time you have, what shape the house is in, and how much you want to spend before closing.

Redmond is a King County city about 15 miles east of Seattle, and the Census Bureau puts its July 2025 population at 82,506. Demand here is tied closely to the tech payroll around the Microsoft campus, so a house near the Overlake or downtown light rail stations often draws a different buyer pool than one on Education Hill or in the outer residential streets. Before you choose a route, decide which of these matters most:

  • A firm closing date, for example because of a move, a job change or a probate deadline.
  • The highest possible price, which usually means repairs, staging and a few weeks of showings.
  • Selling the house exactly as it stands, with the furniture, the deferred maintenance and any unpermitted work.

A cash buyer purchases without waiting on a lender, so the timeline depends mostly on title work and your own schedule. Ask any buyer to put the price, the closing date, who pays closing costs and any credits for repairs in writing so you can compare offers side by side.

sections.h2: What should a Redmond seller know about the city itself?
sections.html:
Redmond sits on the north end of Lake Sammamish, with the downtown core just north of the lake and the Sammamish River running along the west edge of downtown. The city was incorporated on December 31, 1912, and grew from about 11,000 residents in 1970 to 73,256 in the 2020 census. Its borders touch Kirkland to the west, Bellevue to the southwest and Sammamish to the southeast.

Neighborhoods matter to buyers, and a few stand out. Overlake lies southwest of downtown and holds the Microsoft headquarters campus plus apartments and houses. Education Hill sits north of downtown and takes its name from the five schools built there. Newer growth has gone into the downtown and Overlake areas, where the 2 Line light rail now serves the city: the first section opened in April 2024 and the extension to Downtown Redmond opened on May 10, 2025.

Schools shape which families look at a given street. Most of Redmond belongs to the Lake Washington School District, which runs Redmond High School and Nikola Tesla STEM High School. The Bellevue School District covers the southernmost neighborhoods, mainly below NE 40th Street, and the unincorporated English Hill area is in the Northshore School District. When you list or negotiate, name the district for your address, since buyers search by it.

The local economy is dominated by Microsoft, which reported 44,782 employees in Redmond in the city's 2021 financial report, with Meta, Nintendo of America and the Lake Washington School District also among the largest employers. A 2023 figure cited for the city is that about 89 percent of employees of Redmond companies commute in from elsewhere, which keeps interest in nearby housing steady.

sections.h2: How do Redmond housing numbers compare with nearby cities?
sections.html:
Redmond homes are among the higher-priced in the state, and a large share of residents rent. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts figures below put Redmond next to two neighbors in the same county.

The owner-occupied rate of 43.2 percent means more than half of Redmond households rent. That is why many sellers here are former landlords or heirs who inherited a rental, and why the rental and short-term rental rules below are worth reading before you decide.

sections.h2: Does Redmond weather affect how a house sells?
sections.html:
Yes, because buyers and inspectors look for water and heat damage. Redmond has a mild climate with cool, wet winters. Average precipitation peaks in December at 5.45 inches and November is the rainiest month, so roof condition, gutters, crawl spaces and drainage tend to come up in inspections. Snow is uncommon, and the record high is 111 degrees Fahrenheit, set on June 28, 2021.

Washington's seller disclosure form asks directly about these points. Plan to answer questions such as:

  • Has the roof leaked in the last five years?
  • Has the basement flooded or leaked, or has there been standing water or a drainage problem?
  • Were building permits and final inspections obtained for any additions, conversions or remodeling?
  • Are there critical areas, wetlands or floodplains on the property?

Under RCW 64.06.020 the completed form must reach the buyer within five business days after both sides accept a written contract, unless otherwise agreed, and the buyer then has three business days after delivery to rescind unless the right was waived. The statute also says the seller must provide at least one smoke detection device and equip the home with carbon monoxide alarms as the state building code requires.

sections.h2: Do Redmond permits and rental rules matter when I sell?
sections.html:
They can, especially if you added space or have rented the house. Redmond requires a building permit for additions, remodels, garage conversions, decks and accessory dwelling units. Work that needs no permit includes one-story detached accessory structures up to 200 square feet, retaining walls not over 4 feet, and replacing windows in the existing openings. New homes and detached accessory dwelling units must have fire sprinklers, according to the city's residential permits page.

If past work was done without a permit, tell the buyer on the disclosure form. A cash purchase as-is lets you transfer the house without finishing that paperwork, although the buyer will price the risk in. The Development Services counter can tell you what the file shows for your address.

Short-term rentals changed recently. Redmond adopted Ordinance 3239 on December 2, 2025, and a City of Redmond business license for short-term rentals took effect on January 1, 2026, in addition to the state license. The city issues one license per individually addressed rental in single-family areas and one per operator in multifamily or mixed-use buildings. Rentals under 30 consecutive nights are the ones covered, and an owner-occupied home with fewer than three rooms rented for at least six months a year falls outside the definition. Operating without a license carries a penalty equal to 100 percent of the fee, so confirm your standing before you hand over an operating rental.

sections.h2: What taxes and paperwork come with closing a Redmond sale?
sections.html:
The seller usually pays the Washington real estate excise tax, and it is due to the county treasurer where the property sits on the date of sale. The Department of Revenue treats the date the deed is notarized as the date of sale. A graduated state rate applies to the selling price, and a local rate is added on top. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the state brackets are:

  • 1.1% on the portion up to $551,000
  • 1.28% on the portion above $551,000 up to $1,551,000
  • 2.75% on the portion above $1,551,000 up to $3,051,000
  • 3.0% on the portion above $3,051,000

Ask your escrow officer or the King County Recorder's Office for the local rate and the amount for a Redmond address, and for the thresholds that apply to a sale that closes before the new year. If the tax is not paid within one month of the sale, interest starts running, and the Department of Revenue lists an assessment rate of 6 percent for 2026.

Property tax is separate. Under RCW 84.56.020 taxes are due April 30, and half can be paid then with the rest by October 31 when the total is $50 or more. Taxes follow the parcel, so closing should prorate the current year between you and the buyer. Request a tax statement from King County Treasury before you accept a closing date.

sections.h2: How do listing, selling yourself and a cash sale compare?
sections.html:
Each route trades price against speed and certainty. The points below are the ones Redmond sellers weigh most often.

  • Listing with an agent: widest exposure to Eastside buyers, with showings, inspections and repair negotiations before closing.
  • Selling on your own: you keep the commission amount but handle the marketing, the disclosure form, the contract and the excise tax affidavit yourself.
  • Cash sale as-is: fewer steps and a closing date you pick, with an offer that reflects the house's condition.

Whichever you choose, gather the same documents first: the deed, any loan payoff statement, permit records, HOA documents if the home is in an association, and your latest property tax statement. Having them ready shortens every route.

faqs.q: How long does it take to sell a house in Redmond, WA for cash?
faqs.a: It varies by buyer and by title work, so ask for the closing date in writing. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, which usually shortens the timeline compared with a financed listing. Your own deadlines, such as a payoff or probate step, still set the pace.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax when I sell in Redmond?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays, according to the Washington Department of Revenue, and the tax is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. If the seller does not pay, the buyer becomes responsible and the tax can become a lien on the property. Your escrow officer will calculate the state and local amounts.

faqs.q: Do I have to give the buyer a disclosure form in Redmond?
faqs.a: Yes, for most sales of improved residential property, unless the buyer waives it or the transfer is exempt under RCW 64.06.010. The form is due within five business days after a written contract is accepted, and the buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Redmond house that has unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, but you should disclose it. The state form asks whether permits and final inspections were obtained for additions and remodeling. A buyer who purchases as-is will account for the issue in the price. Contact Redmond Development Services to see which permits are on file.

faqs.q: Do I need a business license to sell a Redmond house that was a short-term rental?
faqs.a: A license is needed to operate a short-term rental, not to sell the house. Since January 1, 2026, Redmond requires a city business license for qualifying short-term rentals. If the rental ran without one, resolve any penalty questions with the city's finance office before closing.
